questions.problem:
Find the binormal vector to the curve $r(t)$ at an arbitrary point, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{1}{2}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+2),\sqrt{3},\operatorname{cos}⁡(t+2)⟩, \\ N(t) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(t+2),0,-\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+2)⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ and $N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.
questions.worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
B(t)=T(t)\times N(t).
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}B(t) & =T(t)\times N(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+2),\sqrt{3},\operatorname{cos}⁡(t+2)⟩\times ⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(t+2),0,-\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+2)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\,\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(t+2) & \sqrt{3} & \operatorname{cos}⁡(t+2) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(t+2) & 0 & -\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+2)\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}\sqrt{3} & \operatorname{cos}⁡(t+2) \\ 0 & -\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+2)\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+2) & \operatorname{cos}⁡(t+2) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(t+2) & -\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+2)\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+2) & \sqrt{3} \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(t+2) & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+2)-0,-(-{sin}^{2}⁡(t+2)-{cos}^{2}⁡(t+2)),0-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(t+2)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+2),1,-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(t+2)⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the binormal vector to the curve $r(t)$ at an arbitrary point, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t-1),1,\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t-1)⟩, \\ N(t) & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t-1),0,-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t-1)⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ and $N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.
questions.worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
B(t)=T(t)\times N(t).
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}B(t) & =T(t)\times N(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t-1),1,\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t-1)⟩\times ⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t-1),0,-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t-1)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\,\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t-1) & 1 & \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t-1) \\ -\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t-1) & 0 & -\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t-1)\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}1 & \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t-1) \\ 0 & -\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t-1)\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t-1) & \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t-1) \\ -\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t-1) & -\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t-1)\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t-1) & 1 \\ -\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t-1) & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t-1)-0,-({sin}^{2}⁡(2t-1)+{cos}^{2}⁡(2t-1)),0+\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t-1)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t-1),-1,\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t-1)⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the binormal vector to the curve $r(t)$ at an arbitrary point, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{1}{5}⟨-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t,3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,4⟩, \\ N(t) & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ and $N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.
questions.worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
B(t)=T(t)\times N(t).
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}B(t) & =T(t)\times N(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}⟨-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t,3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,4⟩\times ⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -3\operatorname{sin}⁡t & 3\operatorname{cos}⁡t & 4 \\ -\operatorname{cos}⁡t & -\operatorname{sin}⁡t & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{cos}⁡t & 4 \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t & 4 \\ -\operatorname{cos}⁡t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t & 3\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ -\operatorname{cos}⁡t & -\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}⟨(0-(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t)),-(0-(-4\operatorname{cos}⁡t)),(3{sin}^{2}⁡t+3{cos}^{2}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{5}⟨4\operatorname{sin}⁡t,-4\operatorname{cos}⁡t,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the binormal vector to the curve $r(t)$ at an arbitrary point, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨-\sqrt{t},0,\sqrt{3-t}⟩, \\ N(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨-\sqrt{3-t},0,-\sqrt{t}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ and $N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.
questions.worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
B(t)=T(t)\times N(t).
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}B(t) & =T(t)\times N(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨-\sqrt{t},0,\sqrt{3-t}⟩\times \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨-\sqrt{3-t},0,-\sqrt{t}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -\sqrt{t} & 0 & \sqrt{3-t} \\ -\sqrt{3-t} & 0 & -\sqrt{t}\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\left|\begin{aligned}0 & \sqrt{3-t} \\ 0 & -\sqrt{t}\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}-\sqrt{t} & \sqrt{3-t} \\ -\sqrt{3-t} & -\sqrt{t}\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}-\sqrt{t} & 0 \\ -\sqrt{3-t} & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨0-0,-(t+(3-t)),0-0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨0,-3,0⟩ \\  & =⟨0,-1,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the binormal vector to the curve $r(t)$ at an arbitrary point, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+1}}⟨0,{e}^{t},1⟩, \\ N(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+1}}⟨0,1,-{e}^{t}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ and $N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.
questions.worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
B(t)=T(t)\times N(t).
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}B(t) & =T(t)\times N(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+1}}⟨0,{e}^{t},1⟩\times \frac{1}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+1}}⟨0,1,-{e}^{t}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{{e}^{2t}+1}\,\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & {e}^{t} & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -{e}^{t}\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{{e}^{2t}+1}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} & 1 \\ 1 & -{e}^{t}\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 0 & -{e}^{t}\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}0 & {e}^{t} \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{{e}^{2t}+1}⟨-{e}^{2t}-1,-(0-0),0-0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{{e}^{2t}+1}⟨-({e}^{2t}+1),0,0⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,0,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the binormal vector to the curve $r(t)$ at the point $t=2$, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(2) & =\frac{1}{3}⟨2,-1,2⟩, \\ N(2) & =\frac{1}{3}⟨-1,2,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ and $N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.
questions.worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
B(t)=T(t)\times N(t).
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}B(2) & =T(2)\times N(2) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨2,-1,2⟩\times \frac{1}{3}⟨-1,2,2⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{9}\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & -1 & 2 \\ -1 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{9}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{9}⟨(-2-4),-(4+2),(4-1)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{9}⟨-6,-6,3⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨-2,-2,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the binormal vector to the curve $r(t)$ at the point $t=1,$ given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1) & =\frac{1}{2}⟨-1,1,\sqrt{2}⟩, \\ N(1) & =\frac{1}{3\sqrt{2}}⟨3,-1,2\sqrt{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ and $N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.
questions.worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
B(t)=T(t)\times N(t).
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}B(1) & =T(1)\times N(1) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨-1,1,\sqrt{2}⟩\times \frac{1}{3\sqrt{2}}⟨3,-1,2\sqrt{2}⟩ \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{12}\,\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -1 & 1 & \sqrt{2} \\ 3 & -1 & 2\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{12}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}1 & \sqrt{2} \\ -1 & 2\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}-1 & \sqrt{2} \\ 3 & 2\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{12}⟨(2\sqrt{2}-(-\sqrt{2})),-(-2\sqrt{2}-3\sqrt{2}),(1-3)⟩ \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{12}⟨2\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{2},-(-5\sqrt{2}),-2⟩ \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{12}⟨3\sqrt{2},5\sqrt{2},-2⟩ \\  & =\frac{2}{12}⟨3,5,-\sqrt{2}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{6}⟨3,5,-\sqrt{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(\operatorname{ln}⁡2) & =\frac{1}{5\sqrt{2}}⟨3,5,4⟩, \\ N(\operatorname{ln}⁡2) & =\frac{1}{5}⟨4,0,-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ and $N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.
questions.worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
B(t)=T(t)\times N(t).
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}B(\operatorname{ln}⁡2) & =T(\operatorname{ln}⁡2)\times N(\operatorname{ln}⁡2) \\  & =\frac{1}{5\sqrt{2}}⟨3,5,4⟩\times \frac{1}{5}⟨4,0,-3⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{25\sqrt{2}}\,\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 3 & 5 & 4 \\ 4 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{25\sqrt{2}}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}5 & 4 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ 4 & -3\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}3 & 5 \\ 4 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{25\sqrt{2}}⟨(-15-0),-(-9-16),(0-20)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{25\sqrt{2}}⟨-15,25,-20⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{5\sqrt{2}}⟨-3,5,-4⟩.\end{aligned}

$$

$$
B(t)=T(t)\times N(t).
$$

$$

Find the binormal vector to the curve $r(t)$ at the point $t=1,$ given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1) & =\frac{1}{3}⟨2,2,1⟩, \\ N(1) & =\frac{1}{3\sqrt{5}}⟨-4,5,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ and $N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.
questions.worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
B(t)=T(t)\times N(t).

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}B(1) & =T(1)\times N(1) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨2,2,1⟩\times \frac{1}{3\sqrt{5}}⟨-4,5,-2⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{9\sqrt{5}}\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 2 & 1 \\ -4 & 5 & -2\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{9\sqrt{5}}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 5 & -2\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -4 & -2\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -4 & 5\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{9\sqrt{5}}⟨(-4-5),-(-4-(-4)),(10-(-8))⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{9\sqrt{5}}⟨-9,0,18⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}⟨-1,0,2⟩.\end{aligned}

questions.problem:
Find the binormal vector to the curve $r(t)$ at an arbitrary point, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+4}}⟨t,2,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ denotes the unit tangent vector.
questions.worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
B(t)=T(t)\times N(t),
$$

where the principal normal vector $N(t)$ is given by

$$
N(t)=\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the principal normal $N(t).$ To do this, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{t}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+4}}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+4}}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{4}{({t}^{2}+4)^{3/2}},\,-\frac{2t}{({t}^{2}+4)^{3/2}},\,0⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\frac{1}{({t}^{2}+4)^{3/2}}\sqrt{(4)^{2}+{(-2t)}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{({t}^{2}+4)^{3/2}}\sqrt{16+4{t}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2}{({t}^{2}+4)^{3/2}}\sqrt{{t}^{2}+4} \\  & =\frac{2}{{t}^{2}+4}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we normalize ${T}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{\frac{1}{({t}^{2}+4)^{3/2}}⟨4,\,-2t,\,0⟩}{(\frac{2}{{t}^{2}+4})}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+4}}⟨2,\,-t,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the binormal vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}B(t) & =T(t)\times N(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+4}}⟨t,2,0⟩\times \frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+4}}⟨2,\,-t,\,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+4}\,\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ t & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & -t & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+4}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ -t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}t & 0 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}t & 2 \\ 2 & -t\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+4}⟨0+0,-(0-0),-{t}^{2}-4⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+4}⟨0,\,0,\,-({t}^{2}+4)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,0,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the binormal vector to the curve $r(t)$ at an arbitrary point, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,1,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ denotes the unit tangent vector.
questions.worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
B(t)=T(t)\times N(t),
$$

where the principal normal vector $N(t)$ is given by

$$
N(t)=\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the principal normal $N(t).$ To do this, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\sqrt{(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+{(0)}^{2}+{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡t-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we normalize ${T}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩}{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}})}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the binormal vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}B(t) & =T(t)\times N(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t,1,\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\,\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t & 1 & \operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t & 0 & -\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}1 & \operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 0 & -\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t & \operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t & -\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t & 1 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t-0,-(-(\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}-(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}),-(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,(\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2},\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,2,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the binormal vector to the curve $r(t)$ at an arbitrary point, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{1}{3}⟨2\sqrt{2},-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ denotes the unit tangent vector.
questions.worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
B(t)=T(t)\times N(t),
$$

where the principal normal vector $N(t)$ is given by

$$
N(t)=\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the principal normal $N(t).$ To do this, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{1}{3}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\sqrt{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨0,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\frac{1}{3}\sqrt{(0)^{2}+{(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we normalize ${T}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{\frac{1}{3}⟨0,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩}{(\frac{1}{3})}=⟨0,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the binormal vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}B(t) & =T(t)\times N(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨2\sqrt{2},-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\times ⟨0,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2\sqrt{2} & -\operatorname{sin}⁡t & \operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ 0 & -\operatorname{cos}⁡t & -\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡t & \operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ -\operatorname{cos}⁡t & -\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{2} & \operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ 0 & -\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{2} & -\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 0 & -\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨({sin}^{2}⁡t-(-{cos}^{2}⁡t)),-(-2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t-0),(-2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t-0)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨1,\,2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the binormal vector to the curve $r(t)$ at an arbitrary point, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+4{t}^{2}}}⟨1,0,2t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ denotes the unit tangent vector.
questions.worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
B(t)=T(t)\times N(t),
$$

where the principal normal vector $N(t)$ is given by

$$
N(t)=\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the principal normal $N(t).$ To do this, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+4{t}^{2}}}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2t}{\sqrt{1+4{t}^{2}}})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{4t}{{(1+4{t}^{2})}^{3/2}},\,0,\,\frac{2}{{(1+4{t}^{2})}^{3/2}}⟩ \\  & =\frac{2}{{(1+4{t}^{2})}^{3/2}}⟨-2t,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\frac{2}{{(1+4{t}^{2})}^{3/2}}\sqrt{(-2t)^{2}+{(0)}^{2}+{(1)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2}{{(1+4{t}^{2})}^{3/2}}\sqrt{1+4{t}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2}{1+4{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we normalize ${T}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{\frac{2}{{(1+4{t}^{2})}^{3/2}}⟨-2t,\,0,\,1⟩}{(\frac{2}{1+4{t}^{2}})}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+4{t}^{2}}}⟨-2t,\,0,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the binormal vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}B(t) & =T(t)\times N(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+4{t}^{2}}}⟨1,0,2t⟩\times \frac{1}{\sqrt{1+4{t}^{2}}}⟨-2t,\,0,\,1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{1+4{t}^{2}}\,\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 2t \\ -2t & 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{1+4{t}^{2}}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}0 & 2t \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 2t \\ -2t & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{1+4{t}^{2}}⟨0-0,-(1+4{t}^{2}),0-0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{1+4{t}^{2}}⟨0,\,-(1+4{t}^{2}),\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨0,-1,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the binormal vector to the curve $r(t)$ at an arbitrary point, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{4{e}^{4t}+1}}⟨2{e}^{2t},1,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ denotes the unit tangent vector.
questions.worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
B(t)=T(t)\times N(t),
$$

where the principal normal vector $N(t)$ is given by

$$
N(t)=\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the principal normal $N(t).$ To do this, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2{e}^{2t}}{\sqrt{4{e}^{4t}+1}}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{4{e}^{4t}+1}}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{4{e}^{2t}}{(4{e}^{4t}+1)^{3/2}},\,-\frac{8{e}^{4t}}{(4{e}^{4t}+1)^{3/2}},\,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{4{e}^{2t}}{(4{e}^{4t}+1)^{3/2}}⟨1,\,-2{e}^{2t},\,0⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\frac{4{e}^{2t}}{(4{e}^{4t}+1)^{3/2}}\sqrt{(1)^{2}+{(-2{e}^{2t})}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{4{e}^{2t}}{(4{e}^{4t}+1)^{3/2}}\sqrt{4{e}^{4t}+1} \\  & =\frac{4{e}^{2t}}{4{e}^{4t}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we normalize ${T}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{\frac{4{e}^{2t}}{(4{e}^{4t}+1)^{3/2}}⟨1,-2{e}^{2t},0⟩}{(\frac{4{e}^{2t}}{4{e}^{4t}+1})}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{4{e}^{4t}+1}}⟨1,\,-2{e}^{2t},\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the binormal vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}B(t) & =T(t)\times N(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{4{e}^{4t}+1}}⟨2{e}^{2t},1,0⟩\times \frac{1}{\sqrt{4{e}^{4t}+1}}⟨1,\,-2{e}^{2t},\,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4{e}^{4t}+1}\,\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2{e}^{2t} & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & -2{e}^{2t} & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{4{e}^{4t}+1}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2{e}^{2t} & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}2{e}^{2t} & 0 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}2{e}^{2t} & 1 \\ 1 & -2{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{4{e}^{4t}+1}⟨0+0,-(0-0),-4{e}^{4t}-1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4{e}^{4t}+1}⟨0,0,-(4{e}^{4t}+1)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Find the binormal vector to the curve $\mathbf r(t)$ at an arbitrary point, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+16}}⟨0,t,4⟩, \\ N(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+16}}⟨0,4,-t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $\mathbf T$ and $\mathbf N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
\mathbf B(t) = \mathbf T(t) \times \mathbf N(t).
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}B(t) & =T(t)\times N(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+16}}⟨0,t,4⟩\times \frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+16}}⟨0,4,-t⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+16}\,\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & t & 4 \\ 0 & 4 & -t\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+16}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}t & 4 \\ 4 & -t\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 0 & -t\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}0 & t \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+16}⟨(-{t}^{2}-16),-(0-0),(0-0)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+16}⟨-({t}^{2}+16),0,0⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,0,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Find the binormal vector to the curve $\mathbf r(t)$ at the point $t=\pi$, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(\pi ) & =\frac{1}{5}⟨0,-3,4⟩, \\ N(\pi ) & =⟨1,0,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $\mathbf T$ and $\mathbf N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
\mathbf B(t) = \mathbf T(t) \times \mathbf N(t).
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}B(\pi ) & =T(\pi )\times N(\pi ) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}⟨0,-3,4⟩\times ⟨1,0,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & -3 & 4 \\ 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}-3 & 4 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}⟨(0-0),-(0-4),(0-(-3))⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{5}⟨0,4,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Find the binormal vector to the curve $\mathbf r(t)$ at an arbitrary point, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡4t,2,\operatorname{cos}⁡4t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $\mathbf T$ denotes the unit tangent vector.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
\mathbf B(t) = \mathbf T(t) \times \mathbf N(t),
$$

where the principal normal vector $\mathbf N(t)$ is given by

$$
\mathbf N(t)= \dfrac{\mathbf T'(t)}{\|\mathbf T'(t)\|}.
$$

First, we find the principal normal $\mathbf{N}(t).$ To do this, we calculate $\mathbf T'(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡4t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡4t)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}⟨4\operatorname{cos}⁡4t,\,0,\,-4\operatorname{sin}⁡4t⟩ \\  & =\frac{4}{\sqrt{5}}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡4t,\,0,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡4t⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\sqrt{(4\operatorname{cos}⁡4t)^{2}+{0}^{2}+{(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡4t)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\sqrt{16{cos}^{2}⁡4t+16{sin}^{2}⁡4t} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\sqrt{16({cos}^{2}⁡4t+{sin}^{2}⁡4t)} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\sqrt{16} \\  & =\frac{4}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we normalize $\mathbf T'(t)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{\frac{4}{\sqrt{5}}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡4t,\,0,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡4t⟩}{(\frac{4}{\sqrt{5}})} \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡4t,\,0,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡4t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the binormal vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}B(t) & =T(t)\times N(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡4t,2,\operatorname{cos}⁡4t⟩\times ⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡4t,\,0,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡4t⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\,\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡4t & 2 & \operatorname{cos}⁡4t \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡4t & 0 & -\operatorname{sin}⁡4t\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}2 & \operatorname{cos}⁡4t \\ 0 & -\operatorname{sin}⁡4t\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡4t & \operatorname{cos}⁡4t \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡4t & -\operatorname{sin}⁡4t\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡4t & 2 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡4t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}⟨-2\operatorname{sin}⁡4t-0,-(-{sin}^{2}⁡4t-{cos}^{2}⁡4t),0-2\operatorname{cos}⁡4t⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}⟨-2\operatorname{sin}⁡4t,\,1,\,-2\operatorname{cos}⁡4t⟩\end{aligned}
$$
